land.text: the Aksumite heartland, Tigray and the Eritrean highlands: 'around 960, a queen known as Gudit (also Yodit or Ésato) conquered Aksum'

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Zagwe dynasty'; the Zagwe proper date from 1137 'most likely', with Gudit's line ruling 'for about 40 years' between (Zagwe page). Cliopatria ends Aksum in 946 and starts the Zagwe in 947; this dossier ends at the page's 960 and the zagwe-dynasty dossier takes the heartland in 960.

capitals.name: Aksum (Axum)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Axum; Kubar (after c. 800)'. Kubar's site is unknown, so the dot stays at Aksum and a capital_move event in 800 marks the move. Coordinates from the project gazetteer (places.jsonl 'Aksum').

keyframe_review.note: -50 to 237, 97,004 km2: Tigray and the Eritrean highlands to the coast at Adulis (bbox 38.0-42.4 E, 12.8-15.6 N). The page: 'the kingdom was founded in the 1st century' and the polity 'arose between 150 BCE and 150 CE'; the Periplus (mid-1st century AD) places Aksum in Zoskales's realm. Cliopatria's -50 lies inside the page's range but before its founding century: kept, with the found event at confidence 1.

correction.text: as drawn (the core with western Yemen, 132,994 km2) for c. 200 to c. 275, with the Arabian part hatched as an occupation of Himyarite and Sabaean land: Gedara (c. 200-230) 'was the first king to be involved in South Arabian affairs' and held 'much of western Yemen until a joint Himyarite-Sabean alliance pushed them out'; in the late 3rd century 'Sabaean pressure eventually pushed Aksumite forces back'; from c. 275 to 352 the core alone (the -50 shape)

keyframe_review.note: 238-352: Cliopatria's Arabian holding starts too late (c. 200 on the page) and ends too late (late 3rd century). The Monumentum Adulitanum (c. 240-260) records the Arabian campaigns. The ledger draws c. 200-275 as an occupation of himyarite-kingdom land (the me-06 agent records the reverse).

353-533: the core. Ezana (320s-c. 360) converted c. 324 (infobox 325 or 328); his Beja and Noba campaigns are undated on the pages. Area check: the infobox gives 1,250,000 km2 for 350 against the shape alive in 350, kingdom-of-axum_238 (132,994 km2; ratio 9.4); the infobox figure would cover the whole Horn and eastern Sudan and no page opened describes such an extent, so the shape is kept and the figure treated as inflated; the Beja country and the Eritrean lowlands may belong in a soft tint but no page says so.

correction.text: as drawn (the core with Yemen to Hadhramaut, 392,798 km2) for 520 to 570, but Yemen in direct rule only 520-525 ('Aksum held on to Southern Arabia from 520 until 525 when Sumyafa Ashwa was deposed by Abraha') and in the vassal tint 525-570 (Abraha's 'Himyarite-Aksumite Kingdom', which 'acknowledged the Axumite king's authority and paid tribute'); after the Persian victory at Hadhramaut, which 'marked the beginning of the Aksumite retreat', and the capture of Sana'a in 570 and the Arabian part is Sasanian; the core alone from 571 to 601

keyframe_review.note: 534-601: Cliopatria starts the Arabian holding in 534 (Kaleb's conquest was 520/525-530 on the pages) and keeps it to 601 (the Persians took Yemen 570-578). Area check: the infobox gives 2,500,000 km2 for 525 against the shape alive in 525, kingdom-of-axum_353 (97,004 km2; ratio 25.8; 6.4 against this 534 shape): the infobox figure is inflated for a kingdom the pages place in Tigray, Eritrea and Yemen. The Himyarite row's overlap in 577-601 is the Sasanian-vassal Himyar; the Aksumite part should not be drawn then.

correction.text: the core as drawn until c. 700; from the end of the 7th century without the northern Eritrean plateau and the coast north of Adulis, where 'the Zanafaj Beja entered the Eritrean plateau at the end of the seventh century, which cut the connection to the Red Sea ports'

keyframe_review.note: 602-805: 'The kingdom's slow decline had begun by the 7th century'; coinage ceased 'in the early eighth century'. The Beja loss (ledger 700, confidence 1) is the researcher's reading of the page's sentence; the Beja need a dossier (af-01-x).

correction.text: the core without the northern Eritrean plateau (Beja from the end of the 7th century); the capital 'moved south to a new location called Kubar' after c. 800

keyframe_review.note: 806-935: Cliopatria's keyframe year matches the infobox's capital move 'after c. 800' (ledger 800, confidence 1); no border move is recorded.

correction.text: the core without the northern Eritrean plateau, for 936 to 960 rather than 946: the kingdom 'collapsed under uncertain circumstances around 960' (infobox 'Collapse: 960 AD'; Dil Na'od, last ruler, '917 or 940-960')

keyframe_review.note: 936-946: Cliopatria ends Aksum in 946 and starts the Zagwe in 947; the page's 960 is used for the end, and the zagwe-dynasty dossier (same group) takes the heartland in 960 while its own Lasta core begins in 947.

region.text: Tigray and the Eritrean highlands with the port of Adulis

ledger.note: c. 50 BC: Aksum rises in Tigray. 'the kingdom was founded in the 1st century' and the polity 'arose between 150 BCE and 150 CE'; the Periplus, 'a trading guide which likely dates to the mid-first century AD', places Aksum within Zoskales's realm. Cliopatria's -50 is inside the page's range but earlier than its founding century; Dʿmt (infobox 'Preceded by') had ended centuries before, so the land was nobody's.

region.text: 'much of western Yemen', held under Gedara (c. 200-230) and his successors

ledger.note: c. 200: Aksum crosses to Arabia. Gedara 'was the first king to be involved in South Arabian affairs'; his reign gave 'control of much of western Yemen until a joint Himyarite-Sabean alliance pushed them out'. The year is the start of Gedara's reign as the page dates it; the land was Himyarite and Sabaean (Cliopatria's Sabaeans row borders Aksum 238-282), so it is drawn hatched (rule 4) with himyarite-kingdom as the owner; the me-06 agent records the reverse.

c. 275: the Aksumites leave Arabia. 'Sabaean pressure eventually pushed Aksumite forces back' in the late 3rd century; the Monumentum Adulitanum (c. 240-260) is the last record of the campaigns. The year is the researcher's for 'late 3rd century'; Cliopatria keeps the Arabian part to 352.

region.text: Meroë: 'conquering Meroë under Ezana in 330 for a short period of time'

ledger.note: 330: Ezana at Meroë. Kush infobox 'Axumite capture of Meroë: 330'; the Kush text has an expedition 'after 340' along the Atbara; the Meroë page 'In 350 AD Meroë was destroyed by Axum'; the Ezana page leaves the Meroë stela to Ezana or Ousanas and says 'conclusive evidence ... is not currently available'. Hatched (rule 4); the kingdom-of-kush dossier records the same event.
331: the Aksumite presence at Meroë ends ('for a short period of time'; one year is the researcher's).

region.text: Himyar, West Yemen and its dependencies (Cliopatria's 534 shape reaches Hadhramaut): 'Aksum held on to Southern Arabia from 520 until 525'

ledger.note: 520: Kaleb conquers Himyar. Kaleb's invasion 'occurred around 520' against Dhu Nuwas and 'Kaleb's soldiers eventually routed Yusuf's forces' (Kaleb page); Kaleb 'appointed a Christian Himyarite, Sumyafa Ashwa, as his viceroy and vassal ruler of Himyar' (Himyar page, which dates the conquest '525-530' and the collapse of Himyar to 530); infobox 'Aksumite invasion of Himyar: 518-525'. The pages disagree on the year within 518-530; the Aksum page's 'from 520' is used.

region.text: Himyar: 'Aksumite control of West Yemen continued until c. 525 when Sumyafa Ashwa was deposed by Abraha, who made himself king' (Kaleb page)

ledger.note: 525: Abraha takes Himyar for himself. 'In 525, Abraha deposed the viceroy Sumūyafa Ashwa and declared himself king of a Himyarite-Aksumite Kingdom' (Aksumite-Persian wars page); Procopius reports Kaleb's 'several unsuccessful attempts' to recover it (Kaleb page). Direct rule ends; the vassal relation begins (next event). Cliopatria's Himyarite row is the counterpart for Abraha's kingdom.

region.text: Abraha's Himyarite-Aksumite kingdom, which 'acknowledged the Axumite king's authority and paid tribute' (Kaleb page); Masruq 'continued the Aksumite vice-royalty in Yemen, resuming payment of tribute to the Aksumites' (Himyar page)

ledger.note: 525-570: Yemen as an Aksumite tributary (vassal tint, rule 4). The Himyar page gives no date for Abraha's seizure or death; the Aksumite-Persian wars page dates the seizure 525.

region.text: Yemen: 'The decisive Persian victory at Hadhramaut marked the beginning of the Aksumite retreat'; after 'the capture of Sanaʽa by Sasanian forces' Wahrez reinstated Sayf ibn Dhī Yazan 'as a vassal of the Sasanian Persian Empire'; Persia 're-conquered Yemen by 578, indefinitely ending Aksumite rule outside of Africa'

ledger.note: 570: Wahrez's Persians end Aksumite Yemen. Khosrow I sent Wahrez 'at the head of a small expeditionary force of 800 Dailamite cavalrymen in 570 CE'; Masruq was executed after 'The decisive Persian victory at Hadhramaut'; Sana'a fell and Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan was reinstated 'as a vassal of the Sasanian Persian Empire'. The war resumed '575 or 578' and Persia 're-conquered Yemen by 578' (the end is dated 570 to the first conquest, confidence 2: the page has an Aksumite comeback 575-578 before 'indefinitely ending Aksumite rule outside of Africa'); 'the Aksumites were largely expelled from the Arabian Peninsula, excluding Najran'. The sasanian-empire takes the land (me-06).

region.text: the northern Eritrean plateau and the coast north of Adulis: 'the Zanafaj Beja entered the Eritrean plateau at the end of the seventh century, which cut the connection to the Red Sea ports'

ledger.note: c. 700: the Beja take the northern plateau. The page gives 'the end of the seventh century' and no boundary; the region (Northern Red Sea, Anseba and Gash-Barka) is the researcher's reading. The Beja need a dossier (af-01-x).
c. 800: the capital moves south to Kubar (infobox 'Kubar (after c. 800)'); the site is unknown, so the map's dot stays at Aksum. Cliopatria's keyframe at 806 may mark this.

c. 960: Gudit conquers Aksum. The kingdom 'collapsed under uncertain circumstances around 960' (infobox 'Collapse: 960 AD'); 'around 960, a queen known as Gudit (also Yodit or Ésato) conquered Aksum'; the last ruler Dil Na'od '917 or 940-960'. The Zagwe 'succeeded Aksum in the eleventh or twelfth century (most likely around 1137)', with Gudit's line between; the zagwe-dynasty dossier carries the heartland from 960 because Cliopatria has no row for Gudit. Cliopatria ends the row in 946.

wars.name: Aksumite intervention in South Arabia
wars.outcome: Gedara (c. 200-230) took 'much of western Yemen until a joint Himyarite-Sabean alliance pushed them out'; late in the 3rd century 'Sabaean pressure eventually pushed Aksumite forces back'. Drawn as an occupation.
wars.note: The Himyarite Kingdom page has nothing on the 3rd-century intervention; the dates are the Aksum page's reign dates for Gedara and 'late 3rd century'.

wars.name: Aksumite campaign against Meroë
wars.outcome: 'conquering Meroë under Ezana in 330 for a short period of time'; the Meroë page dates the destruction to 350 and the Kush page an Atbara expedition after 340; the Ezana page calls the evidence inconclusive.

wars.name: Aksumite invasion of Himyar
wars.outcome: Kaleb 'eventually routed Yusuf's forces' (Dhu Nuwas) and installed Sumyafa Ashwa as viceroy; infobox 'Aksumite invasion of Himyar: 518-525'; 'Aksum held on to Southern Arabia from 520 until 525'. Abraha then made himself king and paid tribute.
wars.note: The Himyar page dates the conquest '525-530' and '530'; the Kaleb page 'around 520'; the Aksum page 'from 520'. Dhu Nuwas's Najran massacre is undated on the pages.

wars.name: Aksumite-Persian wars
wars.outcome: Sasanian victory (infobox 'Establishment of Sasanian Yemen'): Wahrez's 800 Dailamites won at Hadhramaut and took Sana'a in 570, killing Masruq ibn Abraha; after Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan's murder a second expedition of 4,000 'reconquered Yemen by 578'; 'Yemen was annexed by the Sasanian Empire as a province' and 'Greater Yemen remained under Sasanian control until the Early Muslim conquests'.
wars.note: The Byzantine Empire is listed among the belligerents on the page (it had rejected Sayf's appeal). Aksumite rule outside Africa ended 'indefinitely'.

wars.name: Gudit's conquest of Aksum
wars.outcome: 'around 960, a queen known as Gudit (also Yodit or Ésato) conquered Aksum'; the kingdom collapsed and Gudit's line 'ruled for about 40 years' (Zagwe page) before the Zagwe.

certainty.note: Every frontier approximate: highland edges and the Red Sea coast; the Arabian holdings (c. 200-275 occupied, 520-525 direct, 525-570 tributary) have no recorded boundary and follow the Cliopatria shapes.

notes:
One state, not two. The brief asked whether the 996-year row is successive states: the Kingdom of Aksum page treats it as one kingdom from the 1st century to c. 960 with one capital move (Kubar, after c. 800); no split, no new slug. Cliopatria's -50 start is inside the page's '150 BCE to 150 CE' range (confidence 1); the end is moved from Cliopatria's 946 to the page's 960, and the zagwe-dynasty dossier (this batch) takes the heartland in 960 while its Lasta core runs from 947.

Arabia. Cliopatria draws Yemen as Aksumite 238-352 and 534-601. The pages give c. 200-275 (Gedara to the Sabaean counter-pressure; drawn as a hatched occupation of himyarite-kingdom land), 520-525 direct rule after Kaleb's conquest, 525-570 Abraha's tributary kingdom (vassal tint), and the Persian conquest of 570-578. The me-06 agent (himyarite-kingdom, sasanian-empire, sabaeans) should carry the reverse events: Himyar occupied c. 200-275, conquered 520, Abraha's kingdom as Aksumite vassal 525-570, Sasanian from 570/578; the Himyarite row 577-601 in Cliopatria is the Sasanian-vassal Himyar and should not overlap an Aksumite Yemen. The brief's 'the 600 shape overlaps a Himyarite row' is resolved by ending Aksumite Yemen in 570.

Area. Infobox 1,250,000 km2 (350) and 2,500,000 km2 (525) against the shapes alive in those years, 132,994 km2 (kingdom-of-axum_238) and 97,004 km2 (kingdom-of-axum_353) (ratios 9.4 and 25.8). No page opened describes an extent beyond Tigray, Eritrea, the Beja country and Yemen; the infobox figures look inflated and the shapes are kept, the Yemen part with the status changes above. Whether the Beja country (Red Sea Hills) and the Sudanese lowlands were Aksumite under Ezana (his titles claim the Beja and Kasu) is undated on the pages and left out.

Capital. Kubar (after c. 800) has no known site; the capital dot stays at Aksum with a capital_move event at 800 (confidence 1). Adulis was the port; its loss is not dated on the page (the Beja cut the route 'at the end of the seventh century').

Counterparts needing dossiers: Beja (beja; af-01-x), Blemmyes/Noba (Kush's side), Dʿmt (predecessor, c. 980-400 BC, not a direct predecessor at -50), Gudit's kingdom (c. 960-1000; folded into zagwe-dynasty for want of a row). Gazetteer: 'Tigray (region)' covers Tigray and all Eritrea, which is wider than the Aksumite heartland; a 'Aksumite heartland' entry limited to Tigray and the Eritrean highlands (Maekel, Debub) would be better. Rulers: the page gives only Gedara, Endybis, Ezana, Kaleb and Dil Na'od with dates; the rulers key is omitted.
